packages.title: RTFO 2025 fifth provisional status QA
facts: RTFO statistics list the 2025 fifth provisional release dated 23 July 2026.
RTFO reporting-year figures are revised through provisional publications before a final publication.
The RTFO measures renewable transport fuel supply annually under the obligation.
Provisional publication status must be preserved when comparing current-year figures.
An RTFO national fuel-supply statistic is not a parcel greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: RTFO versus SAF Mandate boundary QA
facts: The RTFO collection directs SAF Mandate supply data to a separate SAF statistics collection.
RTFO renewable-fuel statistics and SAF Mandate statistics are separate reporting frameworks.
A certificate or obligation record is not the same thing as measured tailpipe or lifecycle emissions.
Reporting-year data can be updated before finalisation.
No parcel value is inferred from mandate-level fuel supply.

packages.title: RTFO certificate and sustainability characteristics QA
facts: RTFO data tables include carbon and sustainability characteristics for renewable fuel receiving RTFCs.
The tables include certificate-related and voluntary-scheme information.
Certificate issuance is an accounting attribute and is not itself a measured emission quantity.
Fuel-supply records require their reporting-year and provisional/final status to be retained.
No property-level emissions value is derived from RTFO certificate data.

packages.title: RTFO incomplete provisional dataset guard QA
facts: Current-year RTFO tables are published provisionally before the complete final dataset.
Earlier 2025 provisional releases explicitly described their datasets as incomplete.
A provisional dataset must not be treated as a final annual total.
Later revisions can change values as additional supplier data are incorporated.
No missing final value is filled by inference.

packages.title: SAF Mandate 2025 fifth provisional status QA
facts: The SAF Mandate statistics collection lists a fifth provisional 2025 release dated 23 July 2026.
SAF supply is measured annually for the SAF Mandate.
Figures are updated and revised in provisional publications before the final publication.
The collection distinguishes current provisional evidence from later final evidence.
National SAF supply is not a parcel emissions measurement.

packages.title: SAF Mandate and RTFO separation QA
facts: SAF Mandate statistics are maintained as their own collection.
RTFO and SAF Mandate statistics should not be merged without preserving scheme boundaries.
Fuel volume, certificate accounting and greenhouse-gas outcomes are different data concepts.
A provisional mandate statistic can be revised.
No local property emissions estimate is inferred from mandate participation.

packages.title: SAF fifth provisional data cutoff QA
facts: The fifth provisional 2025 SAF data tables are based on data available as of 8 July 2026.
The fifth provisional dataset is explicitly incomplete for the year.
The complete and finalised 2025 dataset is scheduled for November 2026.
Data available after the cutoff must not be backfilled into the published provisional release.
No future final value is treated as observed.

packages.title: SAFC balances and trades versus emissions QA
facts: SAF data tables include SAFC balances by obligation period.
They include trades of SAFCs between suppliers and traders.
They include carbon and sustainability characteristics for SAF receiving certificates.
Certificate balances and trades are accounting records, not direct emission measurements.
No parcel-level carbon value is assigned from SAFC trading.

packages.title: UK ETS installation 20 MW scope QA
facts: UK ETS applies to specified regulated activities including combustion at installations above the stated thermal-input threshold.
The current participating guidance identifies total rated thermal input exceeding 20 MW for the combustion scope described.
Municipal and hazardous-waste incineration is treated separately in the stated exception.
Northern Ireland electricity generators remain under the EU ETS under the Ireland/Northern Ireland arrangements.
Scheme scope does not itself establish a parcel emission value.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime reporting and surrender timing QA
facts: Maritime operators must submit a verified annual emissions report by 31 March following the scheme year.
For the 2026 and 2027 scheme years, the combined surrender deadline stated in the guidance is 30 April 2028.
From the 2028 scheme year onward, surrender is due by 30 April in the following year.
Allowance surrender is a compliance quantity tied to verified emissions, not a property measurement.
No parcel value is inferred from maritime compliance timing.

packages.title: UK ETS aviation free-allocation phase-out QA
facts: The aviation compliance guidance states there will be no free allocation to aircraft operators for the allocation period starting 1 January 2026.
The previous aviation allocation framework covered the 2021 to 2025 allocation period.
Aircraft operators use holding accounts for allowance administration.
Allowance allocation is distinct from the operator's verified annual emissions.
No land-parcel emissions value is inferred from aviation allocation status.

packages.title: Aviation allowance-accounting versus emissions QA
facts: Aircraft operators use an Aircraft Operator Holding Account for UK ETS allowance administration.
Authorised representatives can have permissions to surrender allowances.
Free-allocation entitlement and surrender activity are accounting/compliance records.
Accounting records should not be labelled as direct physical emissions measurements.
No parcel-level emissions estimate is produced.

packages.title: UK ETS installation allocation table 2026 QA
facts: The installation Allocation Table covers free allocation for the 2021 to 2026 allocation period.
The table was updated on 17 April 2026 for amendments including Activity Level Changes.
The 2026 scheme year is treated as an extension of the current allocation period for installation free allocation.
Free allocation can change through activity-level processes and is not identical to actual emissions.
No parcel value is inferred from an installation's allowance allocation.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE and USE free-allocation guard QA
facts: Installations joining the 2026 to 2030 Hospital and Small Emitter or Ultra-Small Emitter lists do not receive free allocation in 2026 when the stated condition applies.
The allocation table is an entitlement table rather than a measurement dataset.
Verified activity data can be used to determine allocation for newly eligible cases.
Activity data used for allocation must not be relabelled as current parcel emissions.
No cadastral inference is made.

packages.title: UK ETS Aviation Allocation Table entitlement QA
facts: The Aviation Allocation Table covers the 2021 to 2025 aviation allocation period.
An operator can be absent from the table when the required application was not made or approved.
The table describes entitlement rather than necessarily the quantity ultimately received into an account.
The table was updated in April 2026 for operator changes including transfers and cessation.
Historical aviation allocation entitlement is not a parcel emission measurement.

packages.title: Aviation Allocation Table historical-period guard QA
facts: The Aviation Allocation Table relates to a period ending in 2025.
Current 2026 aviation free allocation has been phased out under the current UK ETS policy.
Historical allocation records must retain their applicable years.
An allocation-table value must not be treated as current verified emissions.
No local property value is inferred.
